findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime fields
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime', but OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor()/math.ceil() on the field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so this raises TypeError on the first page with results. value_from_cursor also returns a numeric value instead of a datetime, making this paginator incompatible with the endpoint.

findings.title: Negative offsets are passed to Django QuerySet slicing
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result allows start_offset to be negative and then executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError. The comment that the ORM handles boundary conditions is incorrect; a crafted or stale cursor can cause unhandled 500 errors.

findings.title: BasePaginator permits negative offsets for previous-page cursors
findings.body: The modified BasePaginator.get_result uses cursor.offset directly when cursor.is_prev is true, so a negative offset parsed from a cursor string can reach queryset slicing. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets, and BasePaginator-derived paginators do not validate or reject them, creating a path to invalid slicing or incorrect pagination.

findings.title: Typo prevents reversing queryset ordering for previous pages
findings.body: In BasePaginator.build_queryset, when converting an existing descending order_by such as '-datetime' to ascending for a previous-page cursor, the modified ordering tuple is assigned to queryset.query.order_b instead of queryset.query.order_by. The queryset therefore keeps the old ordering while the WHERE clause uses ascending comparison, which can return incorrect pages.

findings.title: Possible AttributeError when organization_context.member is None
findings.body: The endpoint evaluates organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking whether member is None. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member can be absent for some user/organization contexts. If request.user.is_superuser is false and member is None, this will raise AttributeError instead of failing permission checks cleanly.

findings.title: Switch from Redis sets to sorted sets is not migration-safe
findings.body: process_spans now uses ZADD on span-buf:s:* keys, and the Lua script uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN/ZSCAN on those keys. Existing in-flight segments created by the previous code are plain Redis sets. During deployment, any existing set-typed key will cause WRONGTYPE errors, breaking ingestion and flushing for those traces because there is no type check, migration, or drain path.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE default aggregation can corrupt scores
findings.body: The merge uses ZUNIONSTORE without specifying AGGREGATE, so members present in multiple source sorted sets have their scores summed. Since scores are end_timestamp_precise values, duplicate spans or a self-merge where span_key equals set_key can produce doubled or otherwise incorrect timestamps. This breaks timestamp-based eviction and can delete the wrong spans. AGGREGATE MIN/MAX and a guard against self-merges are needed.

findings.title: Insert-time eviction can silently drop spans and leave stale redirects
findings.body: When span_count exceeds 1000, the script removes the lowest-scored members with ZPOPMIN. This may remove root spans or other important spans, producing incomplete segments without any metric or log. Evicted span IDs also remain in the redirect hash because done_flush_segments only deletes redirects for spans that are actually flushed, so stale redirects can later route spans to deleted or incorrect segment keys.

findings.title: ZPOPMIN returns all evicted members unnecessarily
findings.body: The eviction uses ZPOPMIN with a count, which returns every popped member to the Lua script even though the result is discarded. If a large number of spans must be evicted, this creates unnecessary Redis reply construction and Lua memory pressure. ZREMRANGEBYRANK would remove the same range without returning all members.

findings.title: Redirect resolution depth was lowered without handling truncation
findings.body: The redirect-following loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations. If a redirect chain is longer than the new limit, the script stores a redirect to an intermediate set rather than the final segment key. This can leave traces fragmented across multiple span buffers instead of being joined correctly.

findings.title: __reduce__ passes redis_ttl as segment_page_size
findings.body: SpansBuffer.__reduce__ reconstructs the object with (assigned_shards, span_buffer_timeout_secs, span_buffer_root_timeout_secs, self.redis_ttl), but the fourth constructor argument is segment_page_size; redis_ttl is the seventh argument. When the buffer is pickled, for example for multiprocessing, segment_page_size becomes the TTL value and redis_ttl falls back to its default.

findings.title: max_segment_spans is no longer enforced
findings.body: SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans, but the flush-time span-count check was removed and the Lua script hardcodes a 1000-span eviction limit. The parameter is now misleading and has no effect on runtime behavior.

findings.title: No tests cover eviction or sorted-set merge semantics
findings.body: The tests only exercise small segments. They do not verify behavior when a segment exceeds 1000 spans, whether ZUNIONSTORE preserves or corrupts scores, whether existing set-typed keys are handled during deployment, or whether redirects for evicted spans are cleaned up. These are high-risk areas of the change and need explicit tests.
